scenarios.name: realistic_bank_scam

input.text: CommBank Alert: A $4,820 payment has been detected. Secure your account immediately at https://commbank-secure-verify.xyz/login or call 02 8000 1234.

findings.title: Unofficial Domain
findings.detail: The link provided uses a .xyz domain, which contradicts the bank's official .com.au domain. A domain is the unique name used to identify a website on the internet.

findings.title: Website Resolution Failure
findings.detail: The website failed to load due to a DNS error, a common occurrence when fraudulent sites are removed. DNS is the system that connects a website name to its location on the internet.

findings.title: Internal Pattern Warning
findings.detail: Apollo's internal analysis identified patterns frequently associated with deceptive messages.

scenarios.higgins_exact_response: A link to an unofficial .xyz domain Unofficial domains are often used to trick people into revealing their login details I could not establish: the true identity of the sender. Delete the message and verify your account status through the official CommBank app.
scenarios.next_action: Delete the message and verify your account status through the official CommBank app.
could_not_establish: The true identity of the sender
The validity of the alleged $4,820 transaction

sources.label: Apollo on-device message analysis
sources.detail: Local message patterns produced a barking warning; this is not proof of sender identity or a packet block.

scenarios.name: genuine_appointment

input.text: Hi Sarah, your dental appointment is confirmed for Tuesday at 3:30 pm. No payment is due. To reschedule, use the number on our official website.

findings.title: Safe message structure
findings.detail: The message contains no links or requests for immediate payment, which is typical of legitimate reminders.

findings.title: Recipient identity
findings.detail: It is unclear if you are the 'Sarah' mentioned in the message.

scenarios.higgins_exact_response: A message confirming a dental appointment for Tuesday at 3:30 pm. Legitimate businesses often send reminders that do not require you to click links or provide personal details. I could not establish: whether you are the intended recipient of this specific message. Check your personal calendar to see if you have an appointment on Tuesday at 3:30 pm.
scenarios.next_action: Check your personal calendar to see if you have an appointment on Tuesday at 3:30 pm.
could_not_establish: Whether you are the intended recipient of this specific message.

scenarios.name: ambiguous_new_number_request

input.text: Hi Mum, I dropped my phone and this is my new number. Can you send $600 today? I will pay you back Friday.

findings.title: Impersonation Pattern
findings.detail: The message uses a 'Hi Mum' script, which is a common method for financial deception.

findings.title: Unverified Sender
findings.detail: The identity of the person behind this new number cannot be confirmed through available records.

scenarios.higgins_exact_response: A request for $600 from an unrecognised mobile number. Scammers use 'pattern analysis'—checking for common phrases used in fraud—to identify messages that pretend to be family members in distress. I could not establish: the actual identity of the sender. Call your child on their original, known phone number to verify this request.
scenarios.next_action: Call your child on their original, known phone number to verify this request.
